blog_description: Engineering notes from the Tinyrack team — what we build, run, and learn.
home_blog_description: Notes on what we build, run, and learn along the way.
home_hero_subhead: Tinyrack builds open-source tools for people who run their own systems — developed in the open, self-hosted first.
home_values_open_source_description: Everything we build starts in a public repository. Code, roadmap, and decisions are open for anyone to read — and anyone to contribute to.
home_values_self_hosting_description: Every tool is built to run on your own hardware, inside your own four walls. Your data belongs on a machine you can unplug.
home_values_simplicity_description: We keep things small and simple — fewer moving parts, readable code, and tools you can understand end to end.
home_work_description: Small, focused infrastructure tools you can run yourself. Every project is developed in the open on GitHub — code, roadmap, and all.
products_description: We're putting together one place to see everything Tinyrack builds. It's not ready yet — in the meantime, our open source is the best way to see what we're working on.
open_source_hero_description: We develop our tools in the open, run them in production, and stand behind them.
open_source_meta_description: Open-source tools we build, run in production, and develop in the open.
open_source_project_dart_packages_descri: Reusable Dart libraries maintained across Tinyrack projects.
open_source_project_design_description: The shared design system for consistent Tinyrack interfaces.
open_source_project_dotweave_description: A cross-platform CLI that syncs dotfiles with git and age encryption.
open_source_project_proxer_description: A reverse-tunnel CLI for HTTP, SSE, and WebSocket services.
open_source_project_tinyauth_description: A lightweight, self-hosted OpenID Connect provider.
site_description: Tinyrack builds open-source, self-hosted infrastructure tools — developed in the open.
